text:
sasha: Heads-up — saw a customer report where websocket sessions got silently closed during a routing flip and the client auto-reconnected. They were billed twice for the same logical stream. :eyes:

maya: ugh. repro steps? do we have logs or a sample trace id?

sasha: repro id in their report: trace=tr_0b9f. Quick summary: client connected to region-a, streaming started, our smart-router moved them to region-b mid-stream (policy: cost-preference fallback), proxy sends CLOSE (302 migrate), client reconnects with resume token. region-b rejects resume -> new session accepted. billing path counted tokens from both sessions (resume failed + new session).

jorge: that sounds like resume idempotency issue. If resume fails we should be able to detect duplication and not double-charge. Is the reject because resume token namespace is region-scoped?

maya: yep, resume token includes a route_id in current encoding. when route flips we drop/translate the route_id and resume lookup fails with "resume-token-mismatch". logs show: ```ERROR resume_lookup failed resume_id=abc123 err=namespace_mismatch route=region-b```

sasha: exact. customer log snippet: ```[2026-03-18T14:22:11Z] session=abc client=10.2.3.4 resume=abc123 -> 403 resume-token-mismatch (origin route-a)```

oliver: from console/UX side customers expect streaming to be seamless across region moves. They also expect billing to not double count. We should show session lineage in the console (session parent id + route transitions) so customers can understand when a session was migrated vs a fresh connect.

maya: short-term mitigation: 1) router should include a grace header on CLOSE with original route hint; 2) make resume lookup consider canonical token (strip route prefix) for N seconds; 3) emit telemetry tag `route_transition=true` and `resume_attempt_result=[ok|mismatch]`.

jorge: agree. Also add a billing dedupe key: if two sessions from same client/ip/user start within Xs with overlapping stream_id, treat as same logical charge and reconcile. That should be conservative.

anna-oncall: what's the rollout risk? if we change resume lookup to be less strict, could a malicious client reuse tokens cross-tenant?

maya: security note — resume token also encodes tenant+nonce. Stripping only route prefix is safe; we won't drop tenant checks. Need unit tests that ensure cross-tenant reject remains.

oliver: console change: add a small badge in the streaming session view: "migrated" and show timeline of route changes + why (policy: cost/latency). Also add a dashboard tile for `resume_mismatch_rate` per region and `duplicate_charge_reconciliations` count. Product will add to customer-facing SLO docs.

sasha: quick patch idea: router CLOSE -> include header `X-Resume-Canonical: <resume_base_id>` and `X-Route-From: region-a`. Then region-b resume handler will consult canonical id fallback for 30s. We can ship as a canary to region-b only.

deploy-bot: NOTE: canary plan created by @sasha -> canary target: region-b edge pool set b1 (5% traffic). Tag: canary/resume-fallback/2026-03-19

jorge: telemetry changes we need for detection: emit `session.lineage.parent_id`, `session.route_from`, `resume.lookup_result`, and increment `billing.duplicate_flag` when we apply dedupe. Also add alert: `resume_mismatch_rate > 0.5%` over 5m in prod.

maya: I'll open an RFC with proto changes for resume token (strip-able prefix) + handler fallback logic. Will also add unit tests and an integration test that simulates route flip.

oliver: I'll draft console mockups for the session timeline and the new dashboard tiles. UX note: show a tooltip: "Grace resume attempts are allowed for N seconds after a router-guided migration."

sasha: very helpful. cc'ing @anna-oncall — please watch canary tomorrow morning and post any anomalies to #incidents.

anna-oncall: will monitor. if we see duplicate billing spike I'll trigger rollback. :+1:

maya: one more edge: what about SSE clients (not websockets)? behavior is different because some proxies do 302 followed by client reconnect without resume support. we should log `protocol=eventsource` when resume_attempts happen and ensure dedupe covers both protocols.

sasha: good catch. add `protocol` field in telemetry.

oliver: timeline: can we target a low-risk canary today, infra permit?

maya: infra ok for small canary. I can have a draft PR by EOD.

sasha: thanks team. I'll update the canary ticket with repro steps and the quick query to watch: ```
# query pseudo
sum(rate(resume_lookup_result{result="mismatch"}[5m])) by (route)
sum(rate(billing_duplicate_reconciliations[10m]))
```

jorge: will also add a Grafana panel to the platform dashboard and a new alert.

sasha: closing out — follow-ups: maya RFC, oliver console mockups, jorge alerts + billing dedupe plan, canary tomorrow. :rocket:
